nobbys-head.name: Nobbys Head
nobbys-head.bio: A convict-built pier leads out to Nobbys Head, a headland with views over the harbour and Stockton Beach.
nobbys-head.hours: Headland grounds weekends and public holidays, 8:00 AM – 4:00 PM
notes: Port Authority of NSW (manages the headland): grounds open weekends and public holidays 8:00-16:00. Whether the Macquarie Pier walkway is open on weekdays is unverified (a third-party guide says daily). Pin HIGH (OSM cape plus Commons median).

fort-scratchley.name: Fort Scratchley
fort-scratchley.bio: An 1882 headland fort and museum with guided tunnel tours, whose guns first fired in anger in 1942.
notes: A$16.50 is the adult guided tunnel tour (concession 11, child 4-14 9.50, family 42); tours at 10:30, 11:30, 1:10, 1:40 and 2:30. Self-guided grounds and galleries price is not stated on the operator pages (a council snippet says free, unverified).
Closed Tuesdays; public-holiday closures (Good Friday, Christmas Day, Boxing Day, New Year's Day) are from a snippet, unverified. Pin HIGH.

newcastle-museum.name: Newcastle Museum
newcastle-museum.bio: A free museum in three historic railway workshops covering local history, BHP steelworks and hands-on science.
notes: Tuesday to Sunday; also open Mondays in NSW school holidays and some public holidays (Labour Day named on the site). General admission free. Pin HIGH.

bathers-way.name: Bathers Way
bathers-way.bio: A 6 km coastal path from Merewether Baths to Nobbys Beach, passing ocean baths and Strzelecki Lookout.
notes: About 3 hours one way (Visit Newcastle). Pin MEDIUM: 3.0 km along the OSM-mapped route from Merewether Baths; the northern 2.8 km to Nobbys is not mapped, so the midpoint rests on the council's 6 km length.
Overlaps ANZAC Walk (a 450 m section of this route); kept as a separate spot because the research marks it kept.

newcastle-ocean-baths.name: Newcastle Ocean Baths
newcastle-ocean-baths.bio: Open-air ocean baths from 1922 near Newcastle Beach, with a grandstand for sunbathing.
newcastle-ocean-baths.hours: Daily; change rooms from 5:30 AM; closed Wednesdays for cleaning
notes: Closed all day every Wednesday for cleaning (council); hours can change with weather, surf or tide. No charge is stated on the council page or Wikivoyage. Pin HIGH.

merewether-ocean-baths.name: Merewether Ocean Baths
merewether-ocean-baths.bio: Merewether's 1935 ocean baths, billed as the largest complex of their kind in the southern hemisphere.
merewether-ocean-baths.hours: Daily; change rooms from 5:30 AM; closed Thursdays for cleaning
notes: Cleaned every Thursday during the season and closed all day then (council). 'Largest in the southern hemisphere' is Wikivoyage's claim, not the council's, so the bio says 'billed as'. Pin HIGH.

bogey-hole-newcastle.name: Bogey Hole
bogey-hole-newcastle.bio: A rock ocean pool carved by convicts at the foot of King Edward Park, a place for a dip.
notes: Named 'Bogey Hole' to match its Wikipedia title (research used 'The Bogey Hole'), so no wiki field is needed. No ticketUrl: no single steward page.
A council snippet (not loaded) says waves can break over the pool at high tide and it has no fixed hours; worth a safety tip. Pin HIGH.

newcastle-art-gallery.name: Newcastle Art Gallery
newcastle-art-gallery.bio: A regional gallery on Laman Street with a free ground-floor permanent collection of Australian art.
notes: Free ground floor is from an AAP article quoted in search (not loaded); special exhibitions are ticketed (about A$20 adult). Tuesday to Sunday per the gallery site (Wikivoyage says 10-5, site used). Pin HIGH.

newcastle-foreshore.name: Newcastle Foreshore
newcastle-foreshore.bio: Harbourside parkland on the old rail yards with a playground and, around Queens Wharf, bars and cafes.
notes: No ticketUrl: open waterfront park. Venue hours were not checked. Pin HIGH (OSM Foreshore Park).

anzac-walk.name: ANZAC Walk
anzac-walk.bio: A 450 m ridgeline walk from Strzelecki Lookout to Bar Beach, with steel soldier silhouettes bearing names.
notes: Silhouettes carry the names of almost 11,000 Hunter Valley servicemen and women (Visit Newcastle); steps at the south end, wheelchair access via Strzelecki Lookout.

Pin MEDIUM and inferred: the route is not mapped under its name; the point is a Commons median about 270 m from Strzelecki Lookout (-32.936809, 151.776891), which the owner may prefer. No ticketUrl: it is part of the Bathers Way council page.

newcastle-beach.name: Newcastle Beach
newcastle-beach.bio: A surf beach right beside the city centre, a short walk from the ocean baths and the harbour foreshore.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach. Lifeguard season not checked. Pin MEDIUM (OSM beach way).

nobbys-beach.name: Nobbys Beach
nobbys-beach.bio: A city beach below Nobbys Head, flanking Macquarie Pier, one of the safer swimming beaches in Newcastle.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach. Lifeguard season not checked. Pin MEDIUM (OSM beach way).

bar-beach-newcastle.name: Bar Beach
bar-beach-newcastle.bio: Regarded by many as the best of Newcastle's city beaches, good for surfing and kitesurfing.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach. 'Best' is Wikivoyage's 'regarded by many' wording. Lifeguard season not checked. Pin MEDIUM (OSM beach way).

fernleigh-track.name: Fernleigh Track
fernleigh-track.bio: A 15.5 km walking and cycling path on a former railway line from Adamstown to Belmont, through bushland.
notes: The council page says 15 km, Wikivoyage 15.5 km (OSM geometry also totals 15.5 km). The lit tunnel in the placement draft was not confirmed and is left out.
Pin MEDIUM: estimated midpoint within about 0.5 km, because the OSM name tags have a roughly 3 km gap.

blackbutt-reserve.name: Blackbutt Reserve
blackbutt-reserve.bio: A 182 ha bushland reserve with free wildlife exhibits, over 10 km of walking trails and a flying-fox colony.
blackbutt-reserve.hours: Wildlife exhibits 10:00 AM – 4:30 PM; picnic areas 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM
notes: Exhibits closed Christmas Day, Good Friday and before 1 PM on Anzac Day. Flying-fox colony is on the Rainforest trail (Wikivoyage). Main entrance off Carnley Avenue, Kotara.
Pin MEDIUM: Wikivoyage's own listing point near the animal exhibits, not cross-checked against an OSM feature.

hunter-wetlands-centre.name: Hunter Wetlands Centre
hunter-wetlands-centre.bio: A regenerated 45 ha wetland at Shortland with walking, cycling and canoe trails, a visitor centre and cafe.
notes: A$9.50 is the 16-and-over price; concession and child 4-15 A$6, family A$25, under 4 free. Closed some public holidays (Anzac Day, Good Friday, Easter Sunday). Free parking.
At Shortland (operator's address, 1 Wetlands Place); Wikivoyage and the placement draft wrongly say Sandgate. Pin HIGH (OSM visitor centre plus Wikivoyage 30 m).

mount-sugarloaf-lookout.name: Mount Sugarloaf Lookout
mount-sugarloaf-lookout.bio: A 412 m summit lookout at West Wallsend with views over Newcastle, Lake Macquarie, Cessnock and Maitland.
notes: No ticketUrl: the lookout's steward is not confirmed. The 412 m height, views and 275 m-1.6 km walks come from a Visit NSW search summary (page not loaded).

NPWS says parts of Sugarloaf State Conservation Area are closed for mining subsidence: stay on formed tracks. Gate times of the access road were not confirmed (an older story reported night closure). Pin MEDIUM (OSM peak).

lake-macquarie.name: Lake Macquarie
lake-macquarie.bio: Australia's largest coastal lake, twice Sydney Harbour's size, with swim spots, lakeside parks and kayaking.
notes: 110 km2; connected to the Tasman Sea by a short channel. The pin is Speers Point Park (a lakeshore visitor point), not the water centroid; Warners Bay, Belmont and Swansea are equally valid access points.

caves-beach.name: Caves Beach
caves-beach.bio: Surf beach famed for sea caves at low tide, ranked ninth in Tourism Australia's 2025 best beaches list.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach (the council's beaches page covers many beaches). Ranking is from the City of Lake Macquarie's visitor page. Tide safety advice (caves unsafe at high tide) is from search results, not a loaded page: worth a tip once confirmed. Pin MEDIUM (OSM beach node).

catherine-hill-bay.name: Catherine Hill Bay
catherine-hill-bay.wiki: Catherine Hill Bay, New South Wales
catherine-hill-bay.bio: A State Heritage-listed village, the oldest in Lake Macquarie, with a patrolled beach and wooden pier.
notes: No ticketUrl: village and public beach. Whether the pier can be walked on was not checked, so the bio only says it is there. Pin MEDIUM (OSM beach relation centroid).

redhead-beach.name: Redhead Beach
redhead-beach.bio: A patrolled surf beach, first of Lake Macquarie's four, with a 24-hour off-leash dog section.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach. Pin MEDIUM (OSM beach node).

blacksmiths-beach.name: Blacksmiths Beach
blacksmiths-beach.bio: A patrolled family beach at the Swansea Channel breakwater, beside the shallow Grannies Pool.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach. The placement's 'ocean baths' claim was not confirmed and is dropped. Pin MEDIUM (OSM surf club building on the beach).

hunter-valley-gardens.name: Hunter Valley Gardens
hunter-valley-gardens.bio: Ten themed gardens and 8 km of paths across 14 hectares on Broke Road in Pokolbin wine country.
hunter-valley-gardens.hours: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM (last entry 4:00 PM); closed Christmas Day
notes: A$39 is the indicative adult (16+) price from ATDW (child 4-15 about A$31); the official ticket page is script-rendered and unreadable, so treat as approximate. Special events (Christmas Lights Spectacular, Mega Creatures) are ticketed separately. Free parking. Opened October 2003.
Pin MEDIUM (OSM park, 1 m).

pokolbin.name: Pokolbin
pokolbin.bio: Lower Hunter vineyards and cellar doors dating from the 1850s, spread across villages with no single centre.
notes: Written as the Hunter district spot as instructed. Suggest folding into Hunter Valley Gardens (-32.775256, 151.294686, 3 km away): a district with no entrance is a weak spot, and the Gardens are its anchor.
Free to visit; tastings may charge per venue (not researched). Hours vary by cellar door (Wikivoyage examples 10-5 / 10-4:30). Needs a car.
ticketUrl is the regional wine-and-tourism body, not a single steward; the owner may prefer none. Pin is Wikipedia's locality point (a district, not an entrance).

cessnock.name: Cessnock
cessnock.bio: A vineyard service town with early 1900s buildings and a heritage walking-tour brochure.
notes: No ticketUrl: town. Marginal: Wikivoyage's Cessnock page is thin and cheaper motels than Pokolbin are its main practical point. Pin MEDIUM (OSM place node, town centre).

morpeth-nsw.name: Morpeth
morpeth-nsw.bio: A historic village on Maitland's outskirts with cafes and boutique shops, best visited Thursday to Sunday.
notes: No ticketUrl: village. Marginal: Wikivoyage has no Morpeth page of its own (redirects to Maitland), so only one counted source. Pin MEDIUM (Wikipedia point).

maitland-nsw.name: Maitland
maitland-nsw.bio: A historic Hunter city of heritage buildings, the Regional Art Gallery and Walka Water Works.
notes: No ticketUrl: city (the council visitor site was not loaded). Maitland Gaol, its biggest draw, is closed (held), so this is marginal; the Art Gallery (10-5, closed Mondays) and Walka Water Works (free, 7 AM-7 PM in daylight saving) were not individually verified. Pin MEDIUM (Wikipedia town point).

wollombi.name: Wollombi
wollombi.bio: A sandstone heritage village on the Great North Road with a courthouse museum, general store and tavern.
notes: No ticketUrl: village. The 1866 courthouse museum charged A$2 per Wikivoyage (2017); hours not verified. Pin HIGH (Wikipedia plus Wikivoyage 40 m).

watagans-national-park.name: Watagans National Park
watagans-national-park.bio: A rainforest park with lookouts, the Gap Creek Falls walk and Aboriginal sites, an hour from Newcastle.
notes: No vehicle entry fee: the park is absent from NPWS's fee-collecting list (camping is charged separately). Roads are unsealed, most need 4WD, no public transport.

NPWS alerts in October 2026: Gap Creek Forest Walk part-closed for rockfall, Heaton Road closed by landslip. Pin is Gap Creek Lookout (OSM viewpoint, MEDIUM) rather than the woodland centroid; Monkey Face Lookout is -33.019838, 151.428267.

stockton-beach.name: Stockton Beach
stockton-beach.bio: A 32 km beach beside the largest moving coastal sand dune in the southern hemisphere, near Birubi Point.
notes: Free on foot (also bikes and horses). Driving on the beach and dunes needs a 4WD beach vehicle permit: A$33 for 3 days, A$88 annual (Worimi Conservation Lands). Guided dune tours cost extra (Wikivoyage mid-2024: about A$40 for Sand Dune Safaris).

Worimi Conservation Lands are owned by the Worimi people and jointly managed with NPWS. Pin is the Birubi Point SLSC at the Anna Bay access (MEDIUM), the visitor access of a long beach, not a centroid.

mount-tomaree.name: Mount Tomaree
mount-tomaree.bio: A steep 2.2 km return climb to the 161 m summit of Tomaree Head, with WWII gun emplacements at the top.
notes: NPWS: Grade 5, suggested 1h30-2h; views to Cabbage Tree and Boondelbah islands; whales May-November. Tomaree National Park is not on the fee-collecting list (no entry fee). A 2025 alert said the lower section is slippery when wet (unverified).
Pin is the summit (OSM peak, HIGH), not the route midpoint.

shoal-bay-nsw.name: Shoal Bay
shoal-bay-nsw.bio: A sweep of calm white sand beside Tomaree Head, five minutes' drive from Nelson Bay.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach and village. Lifeguard patrol dates not found. Pin MEDIUM (OSM beach way centre), replacing a bay centroid in the water.

nelson-bay-nsw.name: Nelson Bay
nelson-bay-nsw.bio: The Port Stephens hub where whale and dolphin cruises leave from the marina, with shore dives nearby.
notes: No ticketUrl: cruises are sold by many operators. Humpbacks pass May-November; resident dolphins are best late November to May (Wikivoyage). Cruise prices were not read (Wikivoyage 2022 lists about A$60-63 for whale watching).
Pin is d'Albora Nelson Bay Marina (OSM, MEDIUM-equivalent; the tool graded it LOW). Absorbs the held Port Stephens self entry.

fingal-bay-nsw.name: Fingal Bay
fingal-bay-nsw.bio: A white-sand patrolled surf beach under Fingal Head, with a whale-watching platform at Barry Park.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach and village. Do not mention the Fingal Spit or any low-tide crossing to Fingal Island (the tourism board and NPWS warn it is dangerous). Pin MEDIUM (OSM beach).

anna-bay.name: Anna Bay
anna-bay.bio: A surf village and gateway to the Stockton Bight dunes at Birubi Beach, with sandboarding and 4WD tours.
notes: No ticketUrl: village, tours sold by many operators. Overlaps Stockton Beach (same Birubi dunes); keep only if the owner wants the village as well as the dunes. Wikivoyage has no separate Anna Bay page (redirects to Port Stephens).
Pin is the OSM village node (MEDIUM-equivalent; tool LOW); the tool's own pick was a bay centroid in the sea.

one-mile-beach.name: One Mile Beach
one-mile-beach.bio: A one-mile white-sand surf beach, patrolled in summer, with a kiosk and picnic reserve behind the dunes.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach; no entry fee (Tomaree National Park is not on the fee list). The wiki title is the suburb article 'One Mile, New South Wales' (from research): check its lead image shows the beach. Pin MEDIUM (OSM beach).

point-stephens-lighthouse.name: Point Stephens Lighthouse
point-stephens-lighthouse.bio: An 1862 lighthouse on Fingal Island with a unique swept tower base, visited by guided boat tour.
point-stephens-lighthouse.hours: Guided boat tours only; contact the operator for dates
notes: A boat-tour stop only: A$120 is Aquamarine Adventures' 'from' price for the 3.5-hour Fingal Island Eco-Walk and Lighthouse Tour (NPWS says contact the operator for dates and price; Moonshadow-TQC Cruises also runs tours). The Fingal Spit crossing is extremely dangerous and has caused drownings: never describe the island as walkable.

The Lighthouse Keepers' Cottages ruins are closed for safety; the lighthouse itself was not stated closed. ticketUrl is the NPWS page because the tour is sold by several operators. Pin MEDIUM (OSM lighthouse).

gan-gan-lookout.name: Gan Gan Lookout
gan-gan-lookout.bio: A 160 m lookout on Gan Gan Hill with 360-degree views over the peninsula, reached by road without a hike.
notes: No ticketUrl: council lookout (council pages are captcha-blocked). On Lily Hill Road, Nelson Bay. Opening times not confirmed (a 2014 snippet said gates 5 AM-9 PM). Height and 360-degree view are the tourism board's. Pin HIGH.

fly-point-nelson-bay.name: Fly Point
fly-point-nelson-bay.bio: An aquatic reserve for snorkelling and shore diving, with sponge gardens and the odd seahorse metres off.
notes: No ticketUrl: no steward page could be verified (NSW DPI and council pages are captcha-blocked). Fishing and collecting are prohibited (sanctuary zone). Snorkelling and staircase advice came from a search summary, unverified.
No Wikipedia article, so no wiki field. Pin LOW-grade: the OSM locality node of the headland itself; no OSM feature for the entry point exists.

australian-reptile-park.name: Australian Reptile Park
australian-reptile-park.bio: A Somersby wildlife park with crocodiles, snakes, wombats and Tasmanian devils, plus daily crocodile shows.
notes: Adult day pass A$53.99 online, A$58.99 at the gate; child (3-15) A$32.99 online / A$36.99 gate; under 3 free. Entry includes meet-and-greets and live shows. Pacific Highway, Somersby; no local bus (Wikivoyage).
Visit time is an estimate. Pin HIGH (OSM attraction 66 m from Wikipedia).

terrigal-beach.name: Terrigal Beach
terrigal-beach.bio: A golden surf beach with a family rock pool at the southern end and an esplanade of cafes and restaurants.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach. Wikivoyage: dogs not allowed, can get overcrowded. Lifeguard dates not found. Pin HIGH.

bouddi-national-park.name: Bouddi National Park
bouddi-national-park.bio: Cliffs, rainforest and beaches near Killcare, with a coastal walk and an early marine protected area.
notes: A$8 is the NPWS park entry per vehicle per day, not per adult. The walk and track pages say it is charged in the Putty Beach area only; no fee at Maitland Bay Information Centre, Little Beach or Tallow Beach.
Maitland Bay Information Centre (174 The Scenic Road, Killcare) is open weekends and public holidays only, about 11 AM-3 PM. Always open but may close for weather or fire.
Pin is that information centre (OSM, MEDIUM-equivalent; tool LOW), not the park centroid. National park: the owner decides destination or spot.

maitland-bay.name: Maitland Bay
maitland-bay.bio: A secluded bay below a steep 2 km return track, where the 1898 PS Maitland wreck shows at low tide.
notes: No fee at the track start (Maitland Bay Information Centre); the A$8 per-vehicle fee applies at Putty Beach only (NPWS). 15-20 minutes down, 30-40 back up; steep with steps. ticketUrl is the NPWS track page (the bay has no page of its own). Pin MEDIUM (OSM beach).

bouddi-coastal-walk.name: Bouddi Coastal Walk
bouddi-coastal-walk.bio: An 8 km walk from Putty Beach to MacMasters Beach with boardwalks, a whale-watching lookout and wildflowers.
notes: NPWS: 3.5-4.5 hours; Putty Beach to Maitland Bay 3 km, Maitland Bay to Little Beach 3.5 km, Little Beach to MacMasters Beach 1.7 km; Gerrin Point lookout for whales; wildflowers in spring. The walk is free, but parking at the Putty Beach end falls under the A$8 per-vehicle park fee; no NPWS fee stated at the MacMasters end.
The placement said 'Killcare to Maitland Bay'; NPWS says Putty Beach to MacMasters Beach. Pin MEDIUM: midpoint of the 4.64 km mapped under the name (not the full 8 km).

brisbane-water-national-park.name: Brisbane Water National Park
brisbane-water-national-park.bio: Sandstone bushland with wildflowers, ancient Aboriginal rock engravings and walking and cycling trails.
notes: A$8 is the NPWS park entry per vehicle per day, not per adult. Girrakool and Somersby Falls picnic areas open 7 AM-8 PM in daylight saving and 7 AM-6 PM otherwise; other areas open at all times but may close for weather or fire.
Pin is Girrakool Picnic Ground (OSM, MEDIUM-equivalent), the main visitor area, not the centroid. National park: the owner decides destination or spot.

pearl-beach.name: Pearl Beach
pearl-beach.bio: A beach village on the edge of the bush where the Patonga walk ends, with picnic spots and small cafes.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach and village. Only NPWS names it (no Wikivoyage or Visit NSW page), so marginal. Pin MEDIUM (OSM beach).

patonga.name: Patonga
patonga.bio: A fishing and holiday village on Brisk Bay near the Hawkesbury's mouth, with fish and chips by the beach.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach and village. Written as on Brisk Bay (Wikipedia), not Brisbane Water as the placement said. Fish and chips tip is NPWS's. Pin MEDIUM (OSM Patonga Beach).

umina-beach.name: Umina Beach
umina-beach.bio: A family beach on the Woy Woy peninsula with calm shallow water, a kiosk, picnic tables and lifeguards.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach. Patrol hours differ between Visit NSW (council lifeguards Monday-Friday, volunteers weekends and public holidays) and BeachSafe; season dates not settled. Pin MEDIUM-equivalent (OSM beach node).

pelican-feeding.name: Pelican Feeding
pelican-feeding.bio: A daily 3:30 pm pelican feed on Pelican Plaza in The Entrance, the self-styled Pelican Capital of Australia.
notes: No ticketUrl: free public feeding, no operator site. The 3:30 PM time and 'free' come from a Burke's Backyard fact sheet and listings, not the council (council and tourism sites were unreadable); Wikivoyage's listing carries no time. Pin HIGH (OSM Pelican Plaza plus Wikivoyage 27 m).

the-skillion.name: The Skillion
the-skillion.bio: A headland lookout an easy walk from Terrigal Beach, with cliff and coast views and whales May to November.
notes: No ticketUrl: public headland reserve. Humpbacks pass May-November (Visit NSW). Any night closure of the car park was not checked. Pin HIGH.

somersby-falls.name: Somersby Falls
somersby-falls.bio: An 800 m return rainforest walk to a three-tier waterfall, with free barbecues and picnic tables.
somersby-falls.hours: 7:00 AM – 8:00 PM daylight saving; 7:00 AM – 6:00 PM otherwise
notes: A$8 is the Brisbane Water NP entry per vehicle per day, not per adult. Steep and slippery in places (NPWS); the descent to the bottom tier is risky (Wikivoyage); picnic area wheelchair accessible. No public transport. Pin HIGH (OSM waterfall).

bulgandry-art-site.name: Bulgandry Art Site
bulgandry-art-site.bio: Aboriginal rock engravings near Kariong, including a headdressed man, wallabies, fish and a canoe.
notes: A$8 is the Brisbane Water NP entry per vehicle per day ('park entry fees apply'); whether it is collected at this car park is not stated. Visitors must not walk on the rock shelf or touch the engravings. No guided tours are offered (none found on the NPWS page). NPWS gives no opening hours, so 'daylight hours' is a descriptor. Pin MEDIUM (OSM archaeological site).

wamberal-beach.name: Wamberal Beach
wamberal-beach.bio: A long surf beach running north from Terrigal, considered one of the best on the NSW east coast.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach. The 'one of the best' line is Wikivoyage's 2015 text only. The wiki title is the suburb article (no beach article): check the lead image shows the beach. Pin MEDIUM-equivalent (OSM beach node).

forresters-beach.name: Forresters Beach
forresters-beach.bio: A surf beach between Terrigal and Bateau Bay, known for its clear water and reef breaks.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach. Marginal: one 2015 Wikivoyage line plus Wikipedia. Research gave the wiki title as 'Forresters Beach'; the cited Wikipedia URL is 'Forresters_Beach,_New_South_Wales', which is used here. Pin MEDIUM (OSM beach).

putty-beach-bouddi.name: Putty Beach
putty-beach-bouddi.bio: A surf beach and campground in Bouddi National Park, where the Bouddi Coastal Walk begins.
notes: A$8 is the NPWS park entry per vehicle per day (applies at Putty Beach, per NPWS), not per adult. ticketUrl is the park page (no page for the beach). No Wikipedia article. Marginal: only NPWS names it.

little-beach-bouddi.name: Little Beach
little-beach-bouddi.bio: A small beach with a walk-in campground, 3.5 km along the coastal walk from Maitland Bay.
notes: No park entry fee at Little Beach campground (NPWS). Also reached by a 750 m gravel trail from the Grahame Drive gate. Maitland Bay to Little Beach is 3.5 km (the placement said 2.5).
Named plainly 'Little Beach' per the naming rule (research used 'Little Beach (Bouddi)'): check for a name clash with other spots. Marginal: only NPWS names it, as a campground.

tallow-beach-bouddi.name: Tallow Beach
tallow-beach-bouddi.bio: A remote beach reached by a steep 1.2 km management trail, with a walk-in campground near Killcare.
notes: No park entry fee at Tallow Beach campground (NPWS); remote, bring all water. No Wikipedia article for this beach (the title 'Tallow Beach' is Byron Bay's), so no wiki field; possible name clash with the Byron Bay beach in the northern-rivers run. Marginal: only NPWS names it.

wyrrabalong-national-park.name: Wyrrabalong National Park
wyrrabalong-national-park.bio: A two-part coastal park holding the Central Coast's last coastal rainforest, with beaches and whale watching.
notes: Free is inferred: the NPWS visitor-info page states no fee and the NPWS fee-list page could not be fetched; confirm. Highlights: The Coast walking track, Bateau Bay Beach picnic area, Crackneck Point lookout.
Pin is Crackneck Lookout (OSM viewpoint, MEDIUM-equivalent; tool LOW) in the southern section, not the northern-section centroid. National park: the owner decides destination or spot.

patonga-to-pearl-beach-walking-track.name: Patonga to Pearl Beach Walking Track
patonga-to-pearl-beach-walking-track.bio: A 3 km one-way bush walk between two beaches, passing Warrah lookout and sandstone caves.
notes: NPWS: Grade 5, 1.5-2 hours one way; park entry fees apply but no figure is given: A$8 is the Brisbane Water NP rate per vehicle per day and may not be charged at the village ends (confirm; consider free if not).
It follows the Great North Walk (existing Sydney spot sydney-64): possible overlap. Pin MEDIUM: midpoint of the OSM firetrail chain (3.15 km).

woy-woy.name: Woy Woy
woy-woy.bio: A Brisbane Water town with waterfront seafood at Fishermen's Wharf and a one-hour scenic ferry round trip.
notes: No ticketUrl: town; the ferry operator and fare were not researched. Train from Sydney about 1 hr 15 min (Visit NSW). Marginal: Wikivoyage calls it a commuter town. Pin is Woy Woy Wharf (OSM ferry terminal, MEDIUM-equivalent; tool LOW).

great-north-road-nsw.name: Great North Road
great-north-road-nsw.bio: A convict-built World Heritage road, walked as a 9 km loop past a quarry and stone buttresses.
notes: NPWS: Old Great North Road World Heritage walk in Dharug National Park, grade 4, 3.5-4.5 hours; built by up to 720 convicts 1826-1836; quarry with convict graffiti. No entry fee is stated for Dharug (NPWS fee-list page not fetched).
Wiki not set: research lists the title 'Great North Road, New South Wales' but its own cited source URL is 'Great_North_Road_(New_South_Wales)'; confirm before setting.
Pin MEDIUM: midpoint of the OSM chain (3.67 km), on the path. Same cluster as Dharug National Park and Wisemans Ferry; the Sydney Great North Walk spot is separate.

wisemans-ferry.name: Wisemans Ferry
wisemans-ferry.bio: A Hawkesbury village with a free cable ferry crossing in use since 1829, and gateway to Dharug National Park.
notes: No ticketUrl: village; the ferry is under contract to Transport for NSW. Crossing takes about 4 minutes. Wikivoyage listings last updated 2016. Pin HIGH (Wikipedia ferry plus Wikivoyage 40 m).

devils-hole-lookout.name: Devils Hole Lookout
devils-hole-lookout.bio: A paved 300 m walk to a platform over the Barrington wilderness, with views to the coast on a clear day.
devils-hole-lookout.hours: Open 24 hours (road can close with snow and ice)
notes: NPWS: 0.3 km return, grade 1, wheelchair-suitable; between Scone and Gloucester (not 'in the Gloucester sector'); view reaches the coast over 90 km east. No entry fee stated for Barrington Tops (fee-list page not fetched). Part of the Barrington Tops area owned by mid-north-coast; placed here per nsw-overlaps.md. Pin HIGH.

gloucester-falls.name: Gloucester Falls
gloucester-falls.bio: A 1.8 km loop through snow gums to lookouts over Gloucester Falls and the Gloucester River gorge.
gloucester-falls.hours: Open 24 hours (access road can close in wet weather)
notes: NPWS: grade 3, 1-1.5 hours; best after rain; picnic area is between Stroud and Gloucester. No entry fee stated for Barrington Tops (fee-list page not fetched). Placed here per nsw-overlaps.md. Pin HIGH (OSM waterfall).

dungog-nsw.name: Dungog
dungog-nsw.bio: A country town with a heritage main street and the James Theatre, Australia's oldest operating cinema.
notes: No ticketUrl: town (the shire council site did not load). Museum hours are Wikivoyage 2023, not the museum's own page. James Theatre's first film was in 1912; blue plaques mark a self-guided heritage walk. Southern gateway to Barrington Tops. Marginal. Pin is Dungog Museum on the main street (OSM, MEDIUM).

yengo-national-park.name: Yengo National Park
yengo-national-park.bio: Remote World Heritage wilderness with Aboriginal engravings, Finchley lookout and views to Mount Yengo.
yengo-national-park.hours: Open 24 hours (4WD needed in wet weather)
notes: No entry fee stated on NPWS (fee-list page not fetched). No public transport; Big Yango precinct is behind locked gates and needs a permit; some access roads cross private land. Mount Yengo is 668 m; park covers 154,328 ha. Single-source (NPWS) keep.
Pin is Finchley Trig Lookout (OSM, MEDIUM), the NPWS-named viewpoint, not the centroid. National park: the owner decides destination or spot.

dharug-national-park.name: Dharug National Park
dharug-national-park.bio: Rugged Hawkesbury bushland with sandstone cliffs, mountain biking, canoeing and camping at Mill Creek.
notes: No entry fee stated on NPWS (fee-list page not fetched). Reached via Wisemans Ferry Road, by car ferry or on foot; camping at Mill Creek and Ten Mile Hollow. Always open but may close for weather or fire.

Pin is Mill Creek Picnic Area (single OSM source, MEDIUM-equivalent; tool LOW). The Old Great North Road is its own entry (great-north-road-nsw); the bio leaves it out to avoid repeating that entry. National park: the owner decides destination or spot.

held.name: Richmond Vale Railway Museum
held.reason: Closed by council order (official site, live: 'closed by council order, pending a review of safety documentation'), and open only about three Sundays a month when it runs. Hold until reopened.
held.facts: Volunteer-run railway and mining museum at the heritage-listed Richmond Main Colliery, about 4 km south of Kurri Kurri; formed 1979. When open: first three Sundays of each month and school-holiday Sundays, gates from 9:30 AM; adults A$16, concession A$11, child 5-15 A$7.50, under 5 free; miniature train rides, canteen. ticketUrl https://www.richmondvalerailwaymuseum.org/ (loaded). Pin -32.85767, 151.4772 (HIGH, OSM museum). Category museum.

held.name: Port Stephens
held.reason: Duplicates Nelson Bay and the headland and beach spots, and is a region/harbour with no visitor point (the only candidates are a water centroid at -32.69864, 152.15538 and Wikipedia's region point -32.699167, 152.123889). Nelson Bay (the tourism board's primary hub) is written instead.
held.facts: Large natural harbour on the Tomaree peninsula; Wikivoyage has a Port Stephens chapter (whale-watching cruises from Nelson Bay May-November, dolphins best late November-May, Fly Point shore diving, Stockton dunes, Mt Tomaree, Gan Gan Lookout, Point Stephens Lighthouse). Tourism site https://www.portstephens.com.au/ (loaded). Category nature, free. Draft bio if the owner wants it: 'A large natural harbour on the Tomaree peninsula, with dolphin and whale cruises from Nelson Bay.' Needs a land pin (Nelson Bay foreshore) first.

held.reason: No usable pin: only about 9.7 km of the 27 km is mapped under the walk's name in OSM, and the NPWS route-map PDF was not read for the true 13.5 km midpoint. Suggest merging with Mount Tomaree and Tomaree National Park (see notes).
held.facts: NPWS: 27 km one way through Tomaree National Park, 2-3 days, Grade 4, Tomaree Head Summit to Birubi; day 1 Tomaree Head to One Mile Beach 18 km, 7-8 hours; toilets at Shoal Bay, Fingal Bay, Barry Park, One Mile Beach. No entry fee (park not on the fee list). ticketUrl https://www.nationalparks.nsw.gov.au/things-to-do/walking-tracks/tomaree-coastal-walk-app (loaded). Fallback on-path point -32.75977, 152.15954 (midpoint of the mapped ways near Fingal Bay, LOW, not the true midpoint). Category hike, icon 🥾, visit 2-8 h. Draft bio: 'A 27 km coastal walk through Tomaree National Park, from Tomaree Head past Fingal Bay to Birubi.' Route map: https://www.nationalparks.nsw.gov.au/-/media/visitor/files/pdf/maps/1-mip-bespoke-pdf-maps/tomaree-coastal-walk-map-a3-pdf-map.pdf

held.name: Tomaree National Park
held.reason: No usable pin: the placement point is a bush centroid, the NPWS entry points (Fingal Beach SLSC, Tomaree Crescent, Tomaree Head carpark) have no resolved coordinates, and the Tomaree Head carpark (-32.715744, 152.186684) is 100 m from the Mount Tomaree spot. Suggest merging the park with Mount Tomaree and the Coastal Walk.
held.facts: NPWS: backdrop to Nelson Bay, Shoal Bay, Fingal Bay, One Mile, Boat Harbour and Anna Bay; 27 km Tomaree Coastal Walk, whale-watching lookouts, Fort Tomaree, beaches; the only place in NSW with rhyodacite outcrops; borders the largest moving coastal sand dune in the southern hemisphere. No entry fee (not on the fee list). Lighthouse Keepers' Cottages ruins closed to pedestrians. ticketUrl https://www.nationalparks.nsw.gov.au/visit-a-park/parks/tomaree-national-park (loaded). Category nature, visit 2-6 h. Draft bio: 'A coastal national park of headlands, whale-watching lookouts, beaches and the 27 km Tomaree Coastal Walk.' Zenith Beach (OSM beach -32.720144, 152.184589) is another NPWS highlight beside Tomaree Head.

Port Stephens, Tomaree Coastal Walk and Tomaree National Park are held. Pokolbin is written as the Hunter district spot as instructed; suggest folding it into Hunter Valley Gardens (3 km apart, the anchor attraction).

Per-vehicle NPWS fees: Bouddi, Brisbane Water, Somersby Falls, Bulgandry, Putty Beach and the Patonga to Pearl Beach walk carry costMin = costMax = 8 as the A$8 per vehicle per day park fee, not an adult price; Bouddi's own pages say it is collected in the Putty Beach area only. Watagans, Tomaree, Dharug, Yengo, Wyrrabalong and the Barrington Tops spots are written free because no fee is stated (Watagans and Tomaree are confirmed absent from the NPWS fee-collecting list; the others are inferred, the list page could not be fetched).

Overlaps and marginal entries for the owner: Anna Bay vs Stockton Beach (same Birubi dunes); Bathers Way vs ANZAC Walk (a section of it); Great North Road vs Dharug National Park vs Wisemans Ferry (one cluster); Patonga to Pearl Beach walk follows the Great North Walk (sydney-64); Little Beach, Putty Beach and Tallow Beach are single-source (NPWS campgrounds); Maitland is marginal while the gaol is closed; Cessnock, Morpeth, Dungog and Woy Woy are marginal town spots.

Name changes from research: 'The Bogey Hole' written as 'Bogey Hole' (its article title); 'Little Beach (Bouddi)' written as 'Little Beach' (naming rule: no qualifier). Possible name clashes: Little Beach and Tallow Beach with spots from other regions.

Wiki fields set only where research confirmed a title that differs from the name. Great North Road and Fly Point have none; Wamberal and One Mile are suburb articles (check the lead image shows the beach); Forresters Beach uses the URL-confirmed 'Forresters Beach, New South Wales'.

Not mentioned anywhere, by decision: the low-tide walk at Fingal Bay or Fingal Spit (dangerous), any Bulgandry guided tours, and a walkable Point Stephens Lighthouse. Hunter Wetlands Centre is at Shortland, not Sandgate. Patonga is on Brisk Bay.
